mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 3-month RSAFS decline, or if the Rank IC of RSAFS decline predicting negative returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market distress, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following a 3-month INDPRO increase, or if the Rank IC of INDPRO increase predicting positive returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint Rank IC of HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease predicting positive returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following a 3-month PAYEMS increase, or if the Rank IC of PAYEMS increase predicting positive returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a disinflationary environment with easing monetary policy, which boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint Rank IC of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decreases predicting positive returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an expansionary regime.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following a 3-month GDPC1 increase during an expansionary regime, or if the Rank IC of GDPC1 increase predicting positive returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
